newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - Call options sold in British Steel.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Call options sold in British Steel.

text.p: Trading activity in UK stock options bearly trickled through by early afternoon on Friday as traders awaited the release of U.S. payroll data for February, dealers said.
The biggest deal was in British Steel where 1,000 July 160 calls were sold at 7-1/2p and will make a maximum 7-1/2p profit at expiry if the underlying shares are below 260p.
British Steel shares were unchanged at 154-3/4p at 1300 GMT.
The main deal in diversified industrials group Tomkins may have been the rolling forward of a bullish position or a long calendar spread.

The deal involved selling 500 March 280 calls at 7-1/2p and buying 500 June 280 calls at 20p. If this was a spread trade then if the underlying shares finish March expiry at 280p, the short calls will be worthless and the long calls will have effectively been bought at 12-1/2p.
The shares then need to go above 292-1/2p in order to make an overall profit. Tomkins shares fell a penny to 284-1/2p.
Elsewhere, there were buyers of put options in Rolls Royce and Glaxo Wellcome who will make money if those shares fall sufficiently.
In Rolls Royce the main deal was the purchase of 500 May 220 puts at 3p. And in the pharmaceuticals group Glaxo Wellcome, 500 April 1000 puts were bought at 9p.
Rolls Royce shares added 2-1/2p to 257-1/2p while Glaxo Wellcome were up 32p to 1081p.
